title: Affine free residue section cohomology comparison
statement: Let W be a scheme, w a point, E an object of its derived category, with the same fixed derived localizations on all schemes and localized open module sites [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-derived-category]. Let U be an affine open containing w and K a bounded cochain complex on its localized module site. Let r: Z -> N and suppose K^j is isomorphic to the free sheaf of rank r(j) in every degree [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Suppose E restricted to U is isomorphic to Q(K). Form P by evaluating K on the terminal over-object (U,id), then form C by extending scalars along W.evaluation U w hwU to kappa(w) [def-weil-residue-field]. For every integer j, derivedFiberCohomology W E j w [def-sc-derived-fiber-betti] is linearly equivalent over kappa(w) to H^j(C). There is no equality between r(j) and the Betti number assumption and no differential vanishing conclusion.

proof.text: Evaluation preserves the support bound. Each supplied free sheaf isomorphism gives a linear equivalence from its terminal-over-object sections to a finite coordinate module, hence a free and flat section module. Convert the upper support bound to IsStrictlyLE and apply the closed upstream CochainComplex.kFlat_of_isStrictlyLE_of_flat; exact filtered colimits and tensor colimit preservation hold in ModuleCat. This proves the K-flat hypothesis of the object-level comparison.
Use the derived-model comparison to identify the derived residue pullback with Q of the associated sheaf of the explicit residue section complex.

Apply DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors. Over the residue field, moduleSpecΓFunctor is an equivalence and preserves homology. Its homology comparison identifies sections of the homology sheaf with homology of the section complex. Map tilde.toTildeΓNatIso.symm directly to cochain complexes and compose with mapHomologicalComplexIdIso; this identifies that complex with C. Compose these isomorphisms and convert the resulting ModuleCat isomorphism to a linear equivalence. The restored theorem keeps the original statement and dependency list.

theorem affineFree_residueSections_cohomologyLinearEquiv
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{v},
      HasDerivedCategory.{v + 1} (SheafOfModules.{v} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ (Y : Scheme.{v}) (U : Y.Opens), HasDerivedCategory.{v + 1}
      (SheafOfModules.{v} ((moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (W : Scheme.{v}) (E : schemeDerivedCategory W) (w : W)
    (U : W.Opens) (hwU : w ∈ U) (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{v} ((moduleRings W.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
    (hb : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ j : ℤ, j < a ∨ b < j → IsZero (K.X j))
    (r : ℤ → ℕ)
    (hrank : ∀ j : ℤ, Nonempty (K.X j ≅ SheafOfModules.free
      (R := (moduleRings W.toRingedSpace).over U)
      (ULift.{v} (Fin (r j)))))
    (he : Nonempty ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{v}
      (moduleRings W.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj E ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)) :
    let F : SheafOfModules.{v} ((moduleRings W.toRingedSpace).over U) ⥤
      ModuleCat.{v} Γ(W, U) :=
      SheafOfModules.evaluation _
      (.op (Over.mk (𝟙 U)))
    letI : F.Additive := inferInstanceAs
      ((SheafOfModules.forget _ ⋙ PresheafOfModules.evaluation _ _).Additive)
    let T := ModuleCat.extendScalars.{v, v, v} (W.evaluation U w hwU).hom
    letI : T.Additive := (ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj _).left_adjoint_additive
    let C := ((F ⋙ T).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K
    ∀ j : ℤ, Nonempty (derivedFiberCohomology W E j w ≃ₗ[W.residueField w]
      C.homology j)
